  • One row per stop: Town, Stop in the first column, then one column per journey.
  • The direction, Route and Codes rows (shaded) are optional.
  • For the other direction, leave a blank row, then start a new table with a row that has only the direction in the first cell.
  • Days: in Excel, use one tab per day named MF, SA or SU. In a CSV, put a row with just MF, SA or SU in the first cell above each day's timetables.
  • NaPTAN, Latitude and Longitude columns after the stop names place the stops on the route map. Leave them empty if you only need the timetable.

  • It's the timetable file: Town, Stop in the first column, a Route row, then one column per journey.

  • Route badges go where journeys start and finish. A plain list of stops with Route, Town and Stop columns also works.

  • Leave a blank row between tables. A row with just a name above a table becomes its heading.
  • Fare triangle: the first place on its own, then each row is the fares from the places above, followed by the next place.
  • Price table: a row of ticket types, then one row per fare. Add a second heading row (e.g. zones) for the grid layout.
  • Write labels like Month* (31 days): a * highlights the row and the brackets go on a second line.
